evidence: maya.hassan received and clicked a suspicious board-pack themed OAuth consent link from an external domain.
The app Northstar Document Sync was unverified, newly created, and used a synthetic redirect URI outside the approved application catalog.
The user granted high-risk delegated scopes including Files.Read.All, Mail.Read, and offline_access.
A non-interactive sign-in and Graph API activity from 203.0.113.219 occurred after consent without a new password failure or malware event.
The app enumerated users, SharePoint sites, drives, and file metadata using Graph API calls.
Sensitive board, executive compensation, and payroll forecast files were accessed and downloaded.
External anonymous sharing links were created for sensitive files.
DLP matched merger, compensation, and payroll sensitive information after the file activity.
Proxy telemetry shows upload activity to fileshare-sync.example.
A service principal credential was added to the app after the file activity, indicating persistence.
recommended_actions: Revoke OAuth consent grants for Northstar Document Sync.
Disable or delete the suspicious service principal and remove newly added credentials.
Revoke refresh tokens and active sessions for maya.hassan.
Review and remove external sharing links created during the incident window.
Confirm whether files were downloaded or exposed externally and notify legal/privacy stakeholders if required.
Block fileshare-sync.example and related infrastructure at proxy, CASB, and DNS controls.
Hunt for the same app ID, redirect URI, publisher, source IP, scopes, and destination domain across the tenant.
Audit all recent OAuth consent grants with high-risk scopes.
Restrict user consent to verified or admin-approved applications.
Escalate to incident response because sensitive business data and persistence are involved.
